milestones.title: Family 017: π has irrationality exponent 2
milestones.milestone_description:
OpenAI's selected statement OAI.PiExponent.main: for every real $
u>2$, some integer $Q\ge2$ makes $q^{-
u}\le|\pi-p/q|$ hold for all integers $p,q$ with $q\ge Q$; and the real supremum of positive exponents admitting infinitely many distinct rational approximations $r$ with reduced denominator $d(r)\ge2$ and $0<|\pi-r|<d(r)^{-
u}$ is $2$. [Exact source](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/lean/ComparatorChallenges/PiExponent.lean).

milestones.title: Bounded-denominator rational approximations form a finite set
milestones.milestone_description:
For every real number $x$ and natural number $N$, the set of rational numbers whose reduced denominator is at most $N$ and whose distance from $x$ is less than $1$ is finite:
$$\{r\in\mathbb Q:r.\mathrm{den}\le N,\ |x-r|<1\}.\mathrm{Finite}.$$
This supplies the finite exceptional set needed when replacing eventual denominator bounds by finiteness statements about rational approximations.

milestones.title: Equivalent natural and integer denominator formulations
milestones.milestone_description:
For every real number $x$, the eventual lower bound at every exponent $\nu>2$ is equivalent whether its threshold and denominators are natural numbers or integers. In both formulations the threshold is at least $2$, the numerator is an arbitrary integer, and the bound is uniform in the numerator:
$$q^{-\nu}\le |x-p/q|\qquad(q\ge Q).$$
This conversion preserves the non-strict approximation inequality and allows results using integer denominators to be reused with natural denominator statements.

milestones.title: An eventual lower bound gives irrationality exponent two
milestones.milestone_description:
Let $x$ be an irrational real number. Assume that for every real $
u>2$ there is a natural threshold $Q\ge2$ such that $q^{-
u}\le |x-p/q|$ for every integer $p$ and natural $q\ge Q$. Then the irrationality exponent defined by the shared approximation predicates is exactly $2$:
$$\mu(x)=2.$$
The exponent is the real supremum of positive exponents admitting infinitely many distinct rational approximations with reduced denominator at least $2$ and strictly positive error below $q^{-
u}$. The upper estimate uses the assumed eventual bound; the lower estimate uses irrationality and Dirichlet approximation.

milestones.title: No arbitrarily large exceptional denominators gives an eventual bound
milestones.milestone_description:
Let $x$ be a real number. Assume that for each real exponent $
u>2$, it is false that every natural threshold $Q$ admits integers $p$ and natural denominators $q\ge Q$ with $|x-p/q|\le q^{-
u}$. Then for each $
u>2$ there is a natural threshold $Q\ge2$ such that all integers $p$ and natural $q\ge Q$ satisfy $q^{-
u}\le |x-p/q|$. This turns an obstruction to arbitrarily large exceptional denominators into the uniform eventual lower bound used by the irrationality-exponent criterion.

milestones.title: Eventual lower bounds make better-than-quadratic approximations finite
milestones.milestone_description: Let $x$ be a real number satisfying the shared eventual lower-bound predicate, and let $\nu>2$ be real. Then only finitely many rational numbers $r$ with reduced denominator at least $2$ satisfy $0<|x-r|<r.\mathrm{den}^{-\nu}$. The hypothesis provides a bound uniform over all integer numerators and all sufficiently large natural denominators.

milestones.title: Every irrational real has infinitely many approximations at exponent two
milestones.milestone_description: For every irrational real number $x$, the exponent $2$ belongs to the set of approximation exponents: there are infinitely many distinct rational numbers $r$ whose reduced denominator is at least $2$ and whose approximation error satisfies $0<|x-r|<r.\mathrm{den}^{-2}$. This records the Dirichlet lower bound in the shared irrationality-exponent definitions.

milestones.title: The eventual approximation bound for pi implies irrationality exponent two
milestones.milestone_description: Assume that for every real $\nu>2$ there is a natural threshold $Q\ge2$ such that $q^{-\nu}\le|\pi-p/q|$ for every integer numerator $p$ and natural denominator $q\ge Q$. Then the irrationality exponent of $\pi$, defined as the real supremum of the positive approximation exponents in the shared definitions, equals $2$. The eventual bound is an explicit hypothesis of this implication.

milestones.title: Polynomial obstruction to a logarithmic antiderivative
milestones.milestone_description:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $P,Q\in K[X]$ be coprime with $Q\ne0$, and let $c\in K$ be nonzero. Then
$$X(P'Q-PQ')\ne cQ^2.$$
Equivalently, the indicated polynomial identity cannot describe a rational antiderivative of a nonzero scalar multiple of $1/X$.

milestones.title: A finite algebraic extension cannot supply a logarithmic antiderivative
milestones.milestone_description: Let $K$ have characteristic zero and let $E$ be a finite-dimensional extension of $K(X)$ in a compatible tower over $K$. Let $d$ and $D$ be compatible $K$-derivations of $K(X)$ and $E$, with $d(X)=1$. For every $x\in E$ and nonzero $c\in K$, $D(x)$ is not the image of $c/X$ in $E$. Thus passing to this finite extension does not remove the simple-pole obstruction.
